ai.title: Jack Dorsey’s Block made an AI model that talks to you like an awkward new friend
ai.brief: You have got to listen to these conversations with Block’s new Dessa AI model. You have got to listen to these conversations with Block’s new Dessa AI model. Jack Dorsey’s Block announced an AI model called Dessa that’s trained “from scratch on nothing but human conversation,” and to show off the model, Block shared chats it has had with humans that can occasionally be a little awkward and uncanny. Take this one , for example, shared by Dessa lead Ragavan Thurairatnam. The conversation between the model and the speaker does have a mostly natural back and forth (though for some reason, the model initially mistakes the speaker for somebody named “Ronaldo”).

sec.title: Inside the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise: Credential theft through Python startup hooks
sec.brief: 0 release was published to the Python Package Index (PyPI) and distributed through official container images. The malicious package added files that Python could execute during normal interpreter initialization. An application did not need to import LiteLLM for the payload to run: starting Python in an affected environment could be enough. Microsoft analyzed two execution paths in the affected wheels: a credential collector launched through a path extension, and a Unix-oriented loader persisted through site-specific configuration. The collector targeted authentication material across developer tools, AI applications, cloud environments, browsers, and infrastructure. A separate database module attempted to read selected credential and model-configuration records from the LiteLLM proxy. Endpoint observations on Windows and macOS matched the recovered collector’s discovery, encryption, and outbound-connection behavior. In one Windows example, a routine Python invocation to install an unrelated dependency activated the collector.
